newsitem.title: USA: Altera shrs jump on order optimism, Q3 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Altera shrs jump on order optimism, Q3 EPS.

text.p: Shares of semiconductor maker Altera Corp rose sharply Thursday after the company reported better-than-expected third quarter profits and noted excess chip inventories have fallen and orders are rising.
The San Jose, Calif.-based chip maker's stock jumped
On Wednesday, Altera said it earned $24.1 million or $0.52 per fully diluted share in the three months ended September 30, up from $23.7 million or $0.51 a share a year ago.
According to First Call, Altera was expected to report a profit of $0.51 a share in the third quarter.
Industry analysts responded to the news by issuing a rash of buy recommendations.

"The problem they've had for the last six to nine months was inventory," said Bear Stearns analyst Nimal Vallipuram, who raised his rating on the stock to buy from attractive. "It led them to trade at a serious discount to their growth rate."
At least five brokerages upgraded ratings on Altera, most citing company comments on inventories and orders.

In a statement accompanying Altera's earnings, President Rodney Smith said the financial results "indicate that the inventory reduction at end customers and their subcontract manufacturers is nearing completion."
Moreover, he said Altera's backlog of orders grew and "September in particular was a month for strong orders."

Hambrecht & Quist analyst Rob Chaplinsky said the improved inventory levels at Altera and its distributors should allow Altera to retain its gross margin while gaining market share because it has an aggressive strategy for lowering prices by passing on savings from cheaper wafers.
Altera makes programmable logic chips, a market shared with Xilinx Inc and to some extent Lattice Semiconductor Corp.
"We believe Altera can grow faster than the overall CPLD market and still retain attractive margins," Chaplinsky wrote.
Altera's sales and earnings more than doubled in 1995 from 1994, but the growth halted about six months ago.
